title: Number of CPF Members Aged 65-67 Still in Employment and Review of Dependants' Protection Scheme to Increase Age Limit of 65
what_it_is: Number of CPF Members Aged 65-67 Still in Employment and Review of Dependants' Protection Scheme to Increase Age Limit of 65

sections.label: CPF members aged 65 to 67 employment
sections.summary: As of 2024, 94,500 CPF members aged 65 to 67, or 33%, are in employment, and in 2021 DPS maximum age coverage rose from 60 to 65.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As of 2024, 94,500, or 33% of Central Provident Fund (CPF) members aged 65 to 67, are in employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In 2021, we raised the maximum age coverage of the DPS from 60 to 65.

sections.label: DPS lapse rates and grace period
sections.summary: DPS lapse rates stayed under 0.2% in the past three years, and lapsed members get at least 60 days grace and a final notice before termination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The DPS lapse rates have held quite steady and low, at less than 0.2% in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Members who have lapsed on their premium payments are given at least 60 days of payment grace period and a final notice before the DPS coverage is terminated.

sections.label: Considering DPS coverage above 65
sections.summary: Above-65 DPS coverage is being considered, aligning with possible retirement age 65 and re-employment age 70 before 2030, though actuarial studies show premiums rise disproportionately beyond 65.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For above 65 coverage, alongside what actuarial studies have been done to align with the Re-employment Age and the suggestion of targeted approach, we are indeed considering this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: At the next bound, some of the measures that we are looking at to see how we can align the coverage with the potential raising of that retirement age to 65 before 2030 and the Re-employment Age to 70 before 2030 – certainly, these are things that we will look at across, as a package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think the actuarial studies done thus far have shown that the premiums do go up quite disproportionately if we try to extend the cover beyond 65.

sections.label: DPS coverage and reinstatement rates
sections.summary: Members without Ordinary Account contributions cannot pay premiums; about 40% of those lapsed as of 31 December 2022 reinstated or started new cover by 31 December 2024, with over two million covered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Thus, they do not have Ordinary Account contributions which could be used to pay for those premiums.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And for those whose DPS coverage lapsed as of 31 December 2022, around 40% of them have reinstated or they have started new cover as of 31 December 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, there are over two million Singaporeans and Permanent Residents who are covered under DPS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And amongst the active CPF members between the ages of 21 and 65, 86% are covered under DPS.
